newsitem.title: INDIA: Samsung Electronics India investment taking longer.
newsitem.headline: Samsung Electronics India investment taking longer.

text.p: The Indian subsidiary of Samsung Electronics Company Ltd, the Korean consumer electronics giant, said on Monday its $200 million investment in the country will be spread over six years, instead of three as initially planned.

"The local conditions have not been conducive to high growth. The market has not grown as per our expectations and it does not justify immediate investment. The total amount will not change, but the time frame has been changed with 2003 as the target year," B.M. Park, managing director of Samsung India Electronics Ltd.
He said that Samsung had invested about $25 million in India, with $20 million in a joint venture with Larsen and Toubro Ltd for telecommunications equipment.
And $5 million was invested in the equity of Samsung India Electronics Ltd (Samsung India), which is 51 percent owned by Samsung Electronics.
On what investments had been put off, Park said that Samsung had decided to delay its colour picture tube venture, and another to manufacture parts and components for colour televisions.

"An annual market of 2 million televisions does not allow for a manufacturing facility that can make 100 million to 200 million parts and components. Once the volumes pick up next year, we will make the investment," Park told reporters in Bombay.

Park said that investments for other manufacturing facilities for televisions, refrigerators, washing machines and air conditioners were on course. He said the company had not decided on whether to manufacture audio systems in India.
